sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Florence, KY?
sections.html:
Florence homeowners can list, sell privately or accept a cash offer, and the Boone County offices that bill taxes and record deeds apply to all three. Florence is a Boone County city in the Cincinnati metro area, and its sellers deal with two layers of local government: the city for permits and rental rules, the county for assessment, tax collection and the deed.

The 2020 census counted 31,946 residents, which made Florence the eighth-largest city in Kentucky and the largest one that is not a county seat. Growth has continued at a slower pace than in Elizabethtown or Georgetown, with the Census Bureau estimating 34,018 residents on July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: How does the Florence housing market compare with nearby Kentucky cities?
sections.html:
Florence has the highest rents and the oldest age profile of the four cities in this group, and its median home value is the second lowest of the four. Nearly one in five residents is 65 or older.

sections.h2: Where is Florence and what drives demand?
sections.html:
Florence sits in eastern Boone County. U.S. Routes 25, 42 and 127 run through the center of the city and reach downtown Cincinnati in about 12 miles, while Interstates 71 and 75 cross the western side with exits 178 through 182.

The area was first called Crossroads, then Maddentown and later Connersville, before taking the name Florence because another Connersville already existed in Harrison County. Growth picked up after the Covington-Lexington Turnpike was finished in 1836, and the city passed 5,000 residents by 1960 and 23,000 by 2000.

Local employers named for Florence include St. Elizabeth Healthcare, Boone County Schools, Robert Bosch, Walmart, Costco and the city itself, with Celanese, Citigroup, Kellogg's and Givaudan operating from nearby addresses outside the city limits. The Florence Y'all water tower, built in 1974, is a landmark for drivers on I-71 and I-75, and the Florence Y'alls baseball team plays at Thomas More Stadium. Turfway Park, a horse racing track, is inside the city limits. Retail sales per person were $69,438 in 2022, the highest of the four cities.

Boone County Schools is the public district listed for Florence, and Gateway Community and Technical College has a campus south of town.

  • The Boone County Public Library has a Florence branch.
  • The Census poverty rate is 9.5% and median household income is $71,003, better than Elizabethtown and Frankfort on both measures.
  • Households average 2.31 people, compared with 2.56 in Georgetown.

sections.h2: What does Boone County put on a Florence property tax bill?
sections.html:
Boone County describes seven tax lines on every bill: the state, the county, the school district, the extension district, the library, the Northern Kentucky Health Department and a fire district. Florence property owners pay a city property tax as well, along with a flat 911 fee of $75 per year for each occupied dwelling, which took effect in 2018.

The county says its bills reach owners each October. The Boone County Property Valuation Administrator is a state office, and the Fiscal Court sets only the county's own rate. Two things set the amount: the assessed value from the PVA and the rate each taxing entity adopts. The sheriff collects the bill and does not set either one.

Read the payment dates printed on your own bill, or ask the Boone County Sheriff. State law moves unpaid bills to the county clerk on April 15 after a 10% penalty and a sheriff's add-on fee, and the clerk adds interest at 1% per month.

sections.h2: Can I challenge a Florence assessment before selling?
sections.html:
Kentucky's appeal process runs on tight deadlines, and the sequence below follows the Department of Revenue's calendar.

  • The tax roll opens for public inspection on the first Monday in May and stays open for 13 days.
  • You must first hold a conference with the PVA or a deputy.
  • After the conference, the appeal is filed at the county clerk's office by the end of the next working day after the inspection period closes.
  • The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after inspection ends and wants documents: sales listings, construction costs, insurance policies and property characteristics.
  • An owner who files and then fails to appear cannot continue to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Homeowners 65 or older and totally disabled owners can apply to the PVA for the homestead exemption, which is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years.

sections.h2: What rental and short-term rental rules apply in Florence?
sections.html:
Many sellers in Florence are landlords, and a buyer who plans to run the house as a short-term rental needs to know that the permit does not transfer. The city defines a short-term rental as a stay of less than 30 consecutive days, requires a separate permit for each property, and grants it only to the applicant at that address.

  • The permit fee is $500, and the host needs at least $1,000,000 in liability insurance.
  • Rentals in most residential zones need a conditional use permit from the Boone County Planning Commission first.
  • Rentals must sit 1,000 feet apart in areas approved by conditional use permit, though the Main Street Overlay District has no spacing rule.
  • Occupancy is capped at two people per bedroom plus two, and events such as weddings are prohibited.

The city lists 859-647-5413 for short-term rental questions. If your house operates as a short-term rental, tell prospective buyers the permit stays with you.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Florence house?
sections.html: An agent makes sense when the house is in good shape and the calendar is flexible. A private sale works with a buyer in hand and an attorney drafting the deed. A cash offer is the practical choice when repairs, tenants, probate or back taxes stand in the way of a financed sale. At the Census median home value of $210,700, the seller's transfer tax under KRS 142.050 is about $211, collected by the county clerk at recording, so the larger costs usually come from the mortgage payoff and repairs.

faqs.q: Do Florence owners pay city property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Boone County says owners in incorporated cities, including Florence, pay a city property tax in addition to the county's seven bill lines. Confirm the amounts on your own bill or with the Boone County Sheriff.

faqs.q: How much is the 911 fee in Boone County?
faqs.a: It is $75 per year for each occupied dwelling, a flat amount that does not depend on assessed value. It began in 2018 and appears on the property tax bill.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Florence short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. The city's permit is granted only to the applicant at the address and cannot be transferred to another person or entity. A new owner has to apply on their own, and most residential zones also need a conditional use permit.

faqs.q: By when must a Boone County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: You have until the close of the working day after the tax roll inspection period ends, and you must hold a conference with the PVA before filing at the county clerk. The inspection period opens the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax would I owe selling a Florence house?
faqs.a: Kentucky charges the seller fifty cents per $500 of value. A house valued at Florence's Census median of $210,700 would owe about $211, collected as the deed is entered in the county record.
